_about: Shared calibration (baseline) test catalogue. Each test: name, category, measure ('number' | 'score' | 'bp'), unit, sides (['L','R'] when measured per side), cap (stop there; the result is then '≥ cap'), rpe/pain (ask for them), flags (yes/no observations, per side), options (for 'score', best first), lib (exercise_lib id for pictures), how (protocol steps), cues, stop (when to stop the test early), gate (a condition that must hold before doing the test), why (what it informs), needs (equipment the test requires), implement (which load_steps list rounds its starting weight). No personal loads or body-specific notes here: the Coach puts those in the person's <data>/plans/calibration.json (field overrides per test, plus their own batteries), see coach/catalogue.py. The batteries below are templates: the Coach copies one, drops tests whose `needs` the person doesn't have or that their profile rules out, and sets loads. Keep test ids stable so retests compare. Rep tests and timed holds are submaximal: stopped at RPE 8 (two reps left, or 'hard but steady') or at the cap, never a max.

bp_rest.name: Resting blood pressure
how: Sit 5 minutes, back supported, feet flat, arm resting at heart height.
Take two readings one minute apart.
bp_rest.stop: 160/100 or higher: rest 5 more minutes and measure again. Still 160/100 or higher: today only the tape measurements and the unloaded mobility tests, no strength tests or timed holds. 180/110 or higher: no exercise; contact your doctor.
bp_rest.why: Session gate and your BP baseline.

waist.name: Waist
how: Tape level around the navel, standing relaxed, at the end of a normal breath out.
waist.why: Fat-loss trend; the best single tape measure.

hips.name: Hips
how: Tape around the widest part of the buttocks, feet together.

chest.name: Chest
how: Tape at nipple level, arms relaxed, at the end of a normal breath out.

arm_flexed.name: Upper arm, flexed
how: Raise the arm to shoulder height, bend the elbow and flex hard.
Tape around the peak of the biceps.
arm_flexed.why: Arm growth, the look you're after.

thigh.name: Thigh
how: Standing relaxed, tape 15 cm above the top of the kneecap.

knee_to_wall.name: Ankle bend (knee to wall)
how: Face a wall in a half-lunge, front foot pointing at the wall.
Keeping the heel down, push the knee forward to touch the wall.
Move the foot back until the knee only just touches with the heel still down.
Measure big toe to wall.
cues: Heel stays glued to the floor
Knee goes over the middle toes
knee_to_wall.why: Squat depth and foot health; under ~10 cm limits squatting.

aslr.name: Straight-leg raise (active)
options: Ankle passes the middle of the other thigh
Ankle between mid-thigh and knee
Ankle below the other knee
how: Right leg first.
Lie on your back, legs straight, arms by your sides, head down.
Lift one straight leg slowly as high as it goes without bending the knee; the other leg stays flat. Don't pull the toes back or lift the head.
Note where the raised ankle is relative to the other leg. The side is the leg you raise.
aslr.stop: Stop at the first stretch you can't hold calmly, or at any change in leg sensation (numbness, tingling, pain travelling down the leg): tick the flag, don't repeat it, and mention it in tomorrow's check-in.
aslr.why: Hamstring and hip mobility, and whether this position irritates a nerve.

shoulder_flex_wall.name: Arm overhead against the wall
how: Stand with heels about 15 cm from a wall; buttocks, upper back and head touching it, low back gently flat.
Raise one straight arm forward and up overhead, slowly, thumb leading.
Measure the gap from the thumb to the wall (0 if it touches) without the low back arching.
shoulder_flex_wall.stop: Move slowly and don't force the end of the range. Stop at pain.
shoulder_flex_wall.why: Readiness for overhead pressing. Pain on either side here means no overhead tests in the strength day.

back_scratch.name: Back scratch reach
how: Reach one hand over the shoulder and down the back; the other hand up the back from below.
Measure the gap between the middle fingertips: a gap is negative, an overlap positive.
The side is the hand on top.
back_scratch.stop: Move slowly and don't force it. Stop at pain.
back_scratch.why: Shoulder rotation; differences between sides matter more than the number.

wrist_wall.name: Wrist extension on the wall
options: Palm flat, elbow straight, no discomfort
Palm flat but with some discomfort
Can't get the palm flat with the elbow straight
how: Stand facing a wall, arm straight at shoulder height.
Place the palm flat on the wall, fingers pointing down, without leaning into it.
Hold 10 seconds.
wrist_wall.why: Readiness for loaded wrist extension: bench, push-ups, front rack.

squat_pattern.name: Bodyweight squat
options: About parallel or lower with a neutral back, heels down
Above parallel with a neutral back
Back rounds or heels lift before parallel
flags: Low back rounds at the bottom
how: Feet shoulder-width, arms straight out in front.
Three slow squats, stopping just above the point where the low back starts to round; no holding at the bottom.
Don't chase depth.

hinge_pattern.name: Hip hinge with a stick
options: Stick stays on head, upper back and tailbone
Loses one contact
Loses two or more
how: Hold a broomstick along your back with one hand at the neck and one at the low back.
Push the hips back and lean forward with soft knees, 5 slow reps, down to where the hamstrings tighten.
hinge_pattern.why: Whether the Romanian deadlift can come in later.

sls_open.name: One-leg stand, eyes open
how: Stand in a room corner or next to something sturdy to grab.
Training shoes, hands on hips.
Lift one foot; time until the foot touches down, the hands leave the hips, or you reach for support.
The side is the standing leg.
sls_open.why: Basic balance; a strong health marker at any age.

sls_closed.name: One-leg stand, eyes closed
how: Same as eyes open, in a corner or next to something sturdy; close the eyes once steady.
sls_closed.why: Balance without vision; very sensitive to change.

sls_pad.name: One-leg stand on the balance pad
how: Eyes open, one foot on the balance pad, in a corner or next to something sturdy.
sls_pad.why: Ankle stability; the starting point for the stability goal.

step_down.name: Step-down control
options: Knee over the middle toes, hips level, smooth
Knee drifts in or a hip drops
Both, or needs the handrail
how: On the bottom step of a house stair, one hand near the handrail. Never use the bench as the step.
Stand on one leg, the other foot hanging off the side.
Slowly lower until the free heel touches the floor, then stand back up. 5 reps.
The side is the standing leg.
step_down.why: Knee and hip control for split squats and step-ups.

side_plank.name: Side plank hold
how: Start from the knees: on the forearm, elbow under the shoulder, knees bent, hips up so knees, hips and shoulders line up. Use the feet version only if 60 s from the knees is already comfortable; write which version in the note.
Hold until it's hard but steady (RPE 8), at the first sag, or the cap. Breathe normally throughout.
The side is the one closest to the floor.
side_plank.why: Lateral trunk endurance; protects the low back.

front_plank.name: Front plank hold
how: On the forearms and toes, body in one line.
Hold until it's hard but steady (RPE 8), at the first sag, or the cap. Breathe normally throughout.
front_plank.stop: Stop at the first sag, if the low back aches, or at any shoulder pain.

sl_bridge.name: One-leg bridge hold
how: On your back, one foot on the floor, the other leg straight in line with the thigh.
Lift the hips level, ribs down; don't arch the back to keep the hips up.
Hold until the hips drop or tilt, or the cap. The side is the working (planted) leg.
sl_bridge.stop: Stop if leg sensation changes. Skip this test if the straight-leg raise changed it today.

polar_fitness.name: Resting fitness test (Polar)
how: On a rested morning this week: lie down, wear the Polar heart-rate strap, start the Fitness test in the Polar app, 5 minutes.
polar_fitness.why: Estimated VO2max; compares with earlier Polar fitness tests.

bench_rm.name: Bench press rep test
how: Spotter arms or safety pins just below chest height. No safeties: do the dumbbell press test instead.
Warm-up: empty bar × 10, then a light set × 5.
Test with a load you could lift about 12–15 times. One set, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 15.
If the warm-up already felt heavy or uncomfortable, test with that load. Enter the load you used.
cues: Bar low in the palm, over the forearm
Stop when a rep slows noticeably
bench_rm.stop: Joint discomfort 3/10 or more ends the test.

db_press.name: Seated dumbbell press rep test
db_press.gate: Only if the overhead and back-scratch tests were pain-free on both sides.
how: Bench at 90°, back on the pad, a pair you could press about 12–15 times; palms facing each other is fine.
One set, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 20. Enter the load you used.
db_press.stop: Shoulder pain 3/10 or more ends the test.
db_press.why: Shoulder strength and press starting weight.

row_cs.name: Chest-supported row rep test
how: Chest on the bench at 30–45°, one dumbbell you could row about 12–15 times, right arm first.
One set per arm, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 20. Enter the load you used.
row_cs.stop: A click with shoulder pain 3/10 or more ends the test (a painless click is fine).

pushup_bar.name: Incline push-up rep test
pushup_bar.gate: Hands on a fixed bar or a sturdy bench. A rack that isn't bolted down: load it with heavy plates, lean on the bar gradually first, and use a bench instead if anything rocks.
how: Hands on a bar at a low setting, or on a bench; write the height in the note so retests match.
One set, chest to the bar or bench, stop with two reps left or at 25.
pushup_bar.why: Pressing endurance with straight wrists. Comes after bench and dumbbell press: keep that order at every retest.

curl.name: Dumbbell curl rep test
how: Warm-up: a light dumbbell × 8 per arm. Then test with one you could curl about 12–15 times. Enter the load you used.
Standing, one arm at a time, elbow still, right arm first.
One set per arm, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 20.
curl.stop: Elbow discomfort 3/10 or more ends the test.

triceps_oh.name: Overhead triceps rep test
triceps_oh.gate: Only if the overhead and back-scratch tests were pain-free on both sides.
how: Seated, back on the pad, one dumbbell in both hands that you could lift about 15 times.
One set, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 25. Enter the load you used.

lateral_raise.name: Lateral raise rep test
lateral_raise.gate: Only if the overhead and back-scratch tests were pain-free on both sides.
how: A light pair (most people start with 2–6 kg), to shoulder height.
One set, stop with two reps left or at 25. Enter the load you used.

suitcase_hold.name: Suitcase hold
how: Stand tall holding a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell at your side (start around a quarter of body weight), slightly away from the feet, not leaning.
Time until the grip is hard (RPE 8) or 60 s. Breathe throughout. The side is the hand holding the weight. Enter the load you used.
suitcase_hold.why: Grip and trunk, side to side. Until there's a grip dynamometer.

goblet_squat.name: Goblet box squat rep test
how: Touch a bench or box behind you each rep, 2 s down, one dumbbell or kettlebell held at the chest that you could squat about 15 times.
One set, stop with two reps left (RPE 8) or at 20. Enter the load you used.
goblet_squat.stop: Any change in leg sensation ends the test and today's lower-body tests.
goblet_squat.why: Leg strength and the squat starting weight.

hip_thrust.name: Dumbbell hip thrust rep test
how: Sit against the bench, place a dumbbell or plate on the hips, then bend the knees and set the upper back on the bench (about 5 s, no long crouch).
Chin tucked, ribs down. One set, stop with two reps left or at 25. Enter the load you used.
hip_thrust.stop: Any change in leg sensation ends the test.

calf_raise.name: Calf raise rep test (both legs)
how: Both legs, flat floor, training shoes (the same shoes every retest), a hand on a wall for balance.
2 s up, 2 s down, full height each rep. Stop at 20 or when height drops.
calf_raise.stop: Any heel or Achilles discomfort: stop and tick the flag.
calf_raise.why: Calf strength; protects the heel and Achilles. Single-leg testing can follow after two weeks of double-leg raises.

wall_sit.name: Wall sit
how: Back flat on the wall, thighs at a comfortable angle (note the angle if not level).
Time until it's hard (RPE 8) or 120 s. Breathe throughout.
wall_sit.why: Leg endurance; isometric work like this also helps blood pressure.

split_squat.name: Split squat rep test
how: First time: bodyweight, a hand on something sturdy for balance. Torso upright, ribs down; the back knee lowers to just above the floor.
One set per leg, stop with two reps left or at the cap. The side is the front leg.

inverted_row.name: Inverted row rep test
inverted_row.gate: A bar at hip height or lower that can't move: a rack's J-hooks or safeties, a Smith machine, or sturdy rings. A rack that isn't bolted down: load it with heavy plates, lean on the bar gradually first, and skip the test if anything rocks.
how: Bar at hip height or lower; write the height setting in the note so retests match.
One set, stop with two reps left or at 20.
inverted_row.why: Bodyweight pulling, the road to a pull-up.

hip_90_90.name: Hip rotation (90/90 sit)
options: Sit tall, both knees close to the floor, no hands
Sit tall only with a hand behind you
Can't sit tall in the position; the back knee or hip lifts well off the floor
how: Sit on the floor: front leg bent 90° in front of you, back leg bent 90° out to the side, both knees bent.
Try to sit tall without hands for 10 s. The side is the FRONT leg.
Swap sides through the middle, slowly.
hip_90_90.stop: A pinch in the front of the hip or any change in leg sensation: stop that side and tick the flag.
hip_90_90.why: Hip rotation both ways; stiff hips push movement into the low back.

thomas_test.name: Hip-flexor length (lying on the bench end)
options: Thigh rests at or below the bench, knee bends about 90°
Thigh level with the bench but the knee straightens
Thigh stays above the bench
flags: Low back arched off the bench
how: Sit in the middle of the flat bench, lower yourself onto your side and forearm, roll onto your back, then slide down until your hips are at the end.

Bring one knee towards your chest only until the low back is flat on the bench, not hard to the chest. Let the other leg hang and relax 5–10 s. Look (or film with the phone) where the hanging thigh rests. The side is the HANGING leg.
To get up: put the hugged foot on the bench, bring the hanging leg up and set that foot on the bench too, roll onto your side and push up with your arms. Never sit straight up.
thomas_test.stop: Back pain or any change in leg sensation: stop and tick the flag.
thomas_test.why: Tight hip flexors tilt the pelvis and arch the low back in standing and squats.

tspine_rotation.name: Upper-back rotation (seated)
options: Shoulders turn past 45° from the knees' line
About 45°
Clearly less than 45°
how: Sit on the bench, knees and feet together and squeezing a rolled towel between the knees so the hips stay still.
Hold a broomstick across the front of the shoulders. Turn slowly as far as is easy, breathing out; no bouncing.
Film from above or have a mirror: compare the stick to the line of your knees. The side is the way you turn.
tspine_rotation.stop: Any pain or change in leg sensation: stop.
tspine_rotation.why: Upper-back rotation; when it's missing, the lumbar spine twists instead.

shoulder_er.name: Shoulder rotation outwards (arm at the side)
options: Forearm turns 70° or more out from straight ahead
Less than 45°
how: Stand with your back to a wall, elbow against your side and bent 90°, forearm pointing straight ahead.
Keep the elbow touching your side and rotate the forearm outwards as far as it goes, slowly. Right arm first.
shoulder_er.stop: Pain 3/10 or more: stop that side.
shoulder_er.why: Rotator-cuff range; side-to-side difference after the 2026 fall and the reported clicks.

trunk_flexor_hold.name: Trunk front hold (lean-back at 60°)
how: Sit on the floor, knees bent 90°, feet flat under the bench (check it doesn't lift; if it does, skip the test).
Hands on the floor behind you, lean back to about 60° from the floor (a third of the way from upright to lying), back straight, not curled. Then cross your arms on your chest.
Hold, breathing normally, until it's hard but steady (RPE 8), at the first drift back or rounding, or at 90 s.
To finish, put your hands back on the floor behind you and push yourself up to sitting. Never lie back and sit up.
trunk_flexor_hold.stop: Any back pain or change in leg sensation: hands down, push up to sitting, tick the flag. Not a sit-up: no curling, never sit up from lying.
trunk_flexor_hold.why: Front trunk endurance; with the side and front planks, the trunk endurance profile that protects the low back.

sit_to_stand_30.name: 30-second chair stand
how: A sturdy chair against a wall; write its seat height in the note so retests match. Arms crossed on the chest, feet flat.
Stand fully and sit fully for 30 s at a quick pace you could keep up, not a sprint. Sit down under control, don't drop onto the chair; breathe out as you stand.
Count full stands.
sit_to_stand_30.stop: Back pain, dizziness or any change in leg sensation: stop.
sit_to_stand_30.why: Leg strength and stamina; one of the best predictors of long-term function.

floor_rise.name: Down to the floor and back up
how: Barefoot, on a mat or carpet, with clear space. From standing, sit down on the floor cross-legged, then stand back up.

Start with 10 points (5 for going down, 5 for getting up). Take off 1 point for each support you use: a hand, a forearm, a knee, the side of a leg, or a hand on your own knee. Take off half a point for a clear wobble.
Use supports freely: this is a score, not a challenge. Move slowly, don't twist to get up; a hand on a bench counts as one support. One try; a second only if the first felt easy.
floor_rise.stop: Left wrist pain 3/10 or more, back pain or any change in leg sensation: stop, write what happened.
floor_rise.why: Strength, flexibility and balance in one move (sitting-rising test); linked with long-term health.

walk_mile.name: 1-mile brisk walk: time
how: A flat, measured 1.6 km (1 mile): a known loop, or track it in the phone or watch app. Wear the heart-rate strap and your usual walking shoes.
5 min easy walk first. Then walk the mile as briskly as you can while still able to speak in short sentences (RPE 7). No running.
Write the time to the nearest 0.1 min (e.g. 14.5).
walk_mile.stop: Chest pain or pressure, dizziness, palpitations or breathlessness out of proportion: stop, sit down, and get medical help if it doesn't settle.
walk_mile.gate: Not on a red recovery day, and resting BP below 160/100.
walk_mile.why: Aerobic fitness you can retest without a lab: the time and heart rate at the same easy-to-repeat effort are your own markers (with the next two values).

walk_mile_hr.name: 1-mile walk: heart rate at the finish
how: Read the heart rate on the strap the moment you finish the mile.
walk_mile_hr.why: Effort at that pace; with the time, an aerobic estimate.

hr_recovery_1min.name: 1-mile walk: heart-rate drop after 1 minute
how: Stand still after the finish and read the heart rate again at exactly 1 minute. Write the DROP (finish minus 1-minute value). If you feel light-headed, sit down and note it.
hr_recovery_1min.why: Heart-rate recovery; a bigger drop means a fitter heart and nervous system.

single_leg_calf.name: Single-leg calf raise rep test
flags: Needed more than a fingertip for balance
how: Flat floor, training shoes, fingertips on the wall for balance only. Right leg first.
2 s up, 2 s down, full height. Stop at 15, when height drops, or at the first heel discomfort.
single_leg_calf.stop: Any heel or Achilles discomfort: stop, tick the flag, skip the other side if it's the heel side.
single_leg_calf.gate: Only if first-step heel pain this morning was 0–1 and the both-legs calf test caused no heel discomfort.
single_leg_calf.why: Left/right calf strength; a weak side loads the plantar fascia.

calibration-1.title: Calibration 1: body, mobility, balance
calibration-1.coach_note: Your baseline, part 1. Not within an hour of waking. Holds stop when they're hard but steady (RPE 8) or at the cap; nothing goes to failure. Measure the same way every time so retests compare: same time of day, same shoes, tape snug but not tight. Stop the session for dizziness, chest pain, or any change in leg sensation; stop any test that sends sensation further down the leg. Skip a test that hurts and write why in its note. Next morning: do the check-in. Rest 1–2 min between the trunk holds (side plank, front plank, trunk front hold, one-leg bridge).

calibration-2.title: Calibration 2: upper-body strength
calibration-2.coach_note: Your baseline, part 2: on a green recovery day, at least a day after part 1, not within an hour of waking. Wear a heart-rate strap if you have one. One test set per lift, stopped with two reps left (RPE 8): a rep that slows noticeably is RPE 8. One test set only; never try a heavier set the same day. Breathe out on every rep. Rest 2–3 min between tests. Respect each test's gate (some depend on part 1). Stop the session for dizziness, chest pain, or any change in leg sensation. Keep this order at every retest. Next morning: do the check-in. It counts as one of that week's sessions.

calibration-3.title: Calibration 3: lower-body strength
calibration-3.coach_note: Your baseline, part 3: on a different day from part 2, on a green recovery day, not within an hour of waking. One test set per lift, stopped with two reps left (RPE 8). Breathe throughout. Rest 2–3 min between tests. Any change in leg sensation ends the lower-body tests for the day. Keep this order at every retest. Next morning: check-in. It counts as one of that week's sessions. Rest at least a day before the next lower-body session.
warmup: Cat-cow × 8, bird dog × 5 / side, glute bridge × 10
Broomstick hip hinge × 8, bodyweight box squat × 8

calibration-4.title: Calibration 4: fitness markers
calibration-4.coach_note: Your baseline, part 4: how well your body handles everyday effort. Not on a red recovery day. Steady efforts, never all-out; keep breathing on every rep. Stop for chest pain, dizziness or breathlessness out of proportion.
warmup: Bodyweight squat to a chair × 5, slow
